parts.title: The World Needs a New Life
The Message of the New Life (The Five Basic Message of the Gospel)

lessons.title: The Goal of the New Life for All People

blocks.label: Scripture Reading
blocks.text: Read John 14:6

Today is the first lesson for the New Life for All People meeting. What is the New Life for All People? What is its goal? There are many people who perceive life as having a lot of money, good houses, good food, good clothes and pleasures: but they do not get any satisfaction. The New Life is more than getting rich or doing something. It is more precious than what we consider to be the special life.
The New Life is the Life of God in Humankind
The life of Jesus Christ Himself. Jesus said, ‘I am... the life’, John 14:6 ‘I have come that you may have life, and have it to the full’, (John 10:10).
If we invite Jesus into our lives, and we allow Him to reveal His life to us, then we have the New Life. The Bible says, ‘Therefore, if anyone is in Christ, the new creation has come:
The old has gone, the new is here!’ (2 Corinthians 5:17).

If we do not have the New Life of Christ, then we live as we please, and our lives reveal these: evil thoughts, carnal desires, idolatry and sorcery, hatred and envy, covetousness and anger (always seeking what is best for yourself), murder, drunkenness, orgies, and things like these. ‘But if the Spirit of Jesus rules our lives, He will manifest in us these fruits: love, joy, peace, long-suffering, gentleness, goodness, faith, meekness, temperance: against such there is no law (Galatians 5:19-23).
The New Life Must Be Proclaimed to Everyone

The purpose of New Life for All People is to make people aware of the life of God in Christ. If we have New Life in Jesus, then we have something precious to share with others who desperately need it. Before Jesus ascended to heaven, He commanded His followers, ‘Go ye into all the world, and preach the gospel to every creature’ (Mark 16:15, KJV). His followers obeyed what He commanded them and turned
the world ‘upside down’ with the gospel of the New Life.

Likewise, we too must obey the Lord’s word and take the gospel of the New Life to everyone. We must show the lost souls what the New Life is – those who need it – why they need it – where to get it – and how to get it.
The Whole Church Must Proclaim the New Life

If everyone everywhere must hear and understand the Gospel, then every Christian MUST be a witness and walk the gospel. All Christians in all denominations should unite in searching for all the lost souls in their country. This implies that you, and not just your pastor, must speak the word. Every believer needs to manifest the New Life at work, in the field, at school and at home.
You Must Preach the Message of the New Life in a Systematic Way

In order for everyone to hear the message of the New Life, we must make good plans to bear witness. Your local Mission Planning group brings all the churches together, and you define a common plan that does not cut off anyone from hearing your case.
We Must Preach the New Life Now

Lately, the devil has been deceiving many people into thinking that holy living is not worth it. They are bound by many bad habits and cannot set themselves free at all. They need the Life of God that will set them free and enable them bear good fruits in their lives. Let us go and begin to introduce them to Christ, who is the source of Life.

verses.text: He who has the Son has life; he who does not have the Son of God does not have life.
but these are written that you may believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God, and that believing you may have life in His name.

blocks.label: Discussion
blocks.text: What do you understand by life or living. How do you think this life will be best for you? Do you believe that all people need this New Life in Christ? Do you believe that it is the duty of every Christian to bear witness? How can you get started right now?

items: Where can we have the light of life? (John 8:12)
How does life in this world come to an end? (1 John 2:15-17)
Why did Jesus Christ come to earth? (John 10:10, John 20:31)
What is the goal of New Life for All People?
What is your responsibility in this New Life for All People (Luke 24:48)?

blocks.label: Revision
blocks.text: Review the answers to last week’s questions.

blocks.label: Scripture Reading
blocks.text: Read Matthew 28:18-20; Acts 1:8, 8:1-6 and ask questions about anything that some members of the group do not understand.
When Jesus Spoke: His last words to His Church, as recorded at Matthew 28:18-20, He emphasised seven (7) things.
Jesus Has All Power (Verse 18)

First, Jesus has authority over each of us. Due to this, if He instructs us to share the gospel with others, we must obey Him. Secondly, it means that the power of Jesus rules over all things including even the devil. Therefore, if we are to bear witness of Him, we must be courageous. We may be overwhelmed by the number of unbelievers, but we are assured in the knowledge that even demons are subject to His authority.
It is the Duty of the Whole Church (Verse 20)

When Jesus gave this command, He was addressing not just the eleven (11) disciples, but the entire Church everywhere and at any time. He says, ‘ and behold, I am with you always, until the end of the world’. Many people today think that it is only the pastor’s job to win souls to Christ, and that the members of the congregation are responsible for paying money to feed the pastors. But Jesus did not command us to leave all the work on the pastors alone. God’s plan is for the pastors to help the church to proclaim the gospel. Ephesians 4:11–12 states that God has given the Church apostles, prophets, evangelists, pastors, and teachers to equip the saints well for the ministry (the missionary work). In Acts chapter 8 we also read that ‘all the church EXCEPT the apostles... walked about preaching the gospel’.

This clearly shows that all Christians must preach. It is impossible for the pastors alone to preach the word to all creation. Also, the members of the congregation have the opportunity to meet many people the clergy will not meet. If we who are not paid preach the message of New Life in Jesus, those who do not know the Lord will think better of it than the words of the clergy.
We Must Go (Verse 19)
First, we must go because we have something that the world does not have - New Life in Jesus, we alone have this gospel.

Secondly, we must go because the world is blinded and lost and cannot find the way to God. Many people who have been lost in sin do not go to church, so we must rise up and go to the streets and marketplaces to find them as Jesus did. We need to go to our neighbours, workmates, and fellow students.
We Must Disciple Others (Verse 19)

To disciple someone means to help someone follow Jesus Christ.The way we do this is to preach the gospel, to call people to repentance from sin, and to follow Jesus as their Lord. As we invite people to Christ, we must not lose sight of the basic foundations of following Jesus. Jesus said, we must ‘hate our family, take up our cross and deny all that we have’. This means that Jesus is more important to us than our relatives, our desires, and all our possessions; otherwise, we cannot be His disciples. (Luke 14:26, 27, 33).
We Must Get New Convert Baptised (Verse 19)
All new disciples of Jesus must be baptised. Water baptism must be by immersion as evidence that the same person has openly accepted Christ publicly and has also joined the church.
We Must Teach New Convert (Verse 20)

It is not enough for people to become followers of Jesus or to join a church. They must also be taught to observe all the commandments of Christ. Note also that what we are to teach is not what they want to hear or what we ourselves want to say but what Christ taught – this teaching is in the Scriptures. We must teach and preach the gospel of Christ in the temple and in houses daily, as the early disciples did (Acts 5:42).
In All These Things That We Should Do, We Have the Promise of the Presence and Power of Christ (Verse 20)

Jesus says, ‘I am with you’. Through the Holy Spirit – the Holy Spirit is with us to guide, strengthen, and empower us. Without Jesus, and His power in our lives, we can do nothing (John 15:5). But if we obey the Great Commandment and reach out to lost souls, we will receive His promise to be with us and the power He provides.

The Great Commission Is God’s Plan For His Church: It is His plan by which we shall reach the lost world. This is also the whole purpose of New Life for All of People – to move every Christian believer in Ghana to witness for Christ in the power and authority of the Holy Spirit. Christians of all denominations should unite to search for all the lost souls of Ghana. This means that you too should be obedient to the Lord’s commandments.

verses.text: But you are a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, His own special people, that you may proclaim the praises of Him who called you out of darkness into His marvelous light

blocks.label: Discussion
blocks.text: Why is it important that all members of the Christian congregation bear witness? List some of the places where we can go to witness.

items: Who has all authority (Matthew 28:18)?
Why has God chosen us? (John 15:16, 1 Peter 2:9)
To whom does God give His Holy Spirit? (Acts 5:32)..
Will you obey the Lord’s commandments?

blocks.label: Revision
blocks.text: Discuss the answers to the previous week’s questions.

blocks.label: Scripture Reading
blocks.text: Read Genesis (Genesis 1:26-28; 2:7-17 and ask questions about anything that is a little difficult to understand.

We Have Met Today Again to start the New Life for All People course: Why do we live? Where does man come from; and how did life begin? The Scriptures say: ‘In the beginning, God created everything, including our planet. He created humankind last.
God is the Giver of Life, and He Gives People All the Good Things
Humans are endowed with knowledge. They are able to invent sophisticated machines, and manufacture many beautiful things, but as for life, humans did not create it, and cannot manufacture it.
Read James 1:17 and describes the names of the things God has given to humankind (see Genesis 1:26; 2:8-14). Everything God made was good (Genesis 1:31).
Humankind is Like God

God created humankind ‘in His own image, to be like Him’. This does not mean that God is like a real person (with two eyes and so on). This means that humans are like God in some ways. Some of the ways in which humans are like God are:
a. God’s ability to care for himself and others; humans also have this gift of caring.
b. God makes a clear distinction between good and evil: the human conscience is able to distinguish between good and evil.
c. God is independent and able to do whatever He pleases. Humans cannot do all that God can, but they are free to do what they want; and for whatever they do, they will be held accountable.

d. God makes friends with the people He has created, and humans can communicate with God just as they can with other people. Therefore, humans, unlike animals, can commune with God and they can also be obedient to God.
In Different Circumstances, Humans Are Totally Different from God
a. God is Holy, which means He does only good. Human nature is the exact opposite; as for humans, they often do what is not good.
b. God is always everywhere, but humans are limited to particular places at particular times.
The Position of Humankind in Creation

If you travel and have someone perform your duty in your absence, you will ask him or her to give an account of all that he or she did when you come back. That is exactly how God has given us our will, but at the same time, He has given us laws to obey. In the future we will be held accountable for the way we used our freedom (Romans 14:12). God does not command us to obey His laws. He gives us commandments and leaves us to decide whether we will obey them or not. But the wages of disobedience is death (Genesis 2:17); that is, we lose the life that God gave us.
We Are the Children of Adam
We, too, were made ‘in the image of God’. He has entrusted us with many things. We too have commandments that we must obey, and for our disobedience, we receive the penalty of death.

verses.text: Every good gift and every perfect gift is from above, and comes down from the Father of lights, with whom there is no variation or shadow of turning.
And the LORD God formed man of the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living being.

blocks.label: Discussion
blocks.text: What does it mean that God created humankind in His own image? Why do you think God created humankind? Look around and point out the things that humans have made and things made by God.

items: How did life come about?
Did God create something that was bad?
What is the punishment for disobedience to God’s commandments?
Write a verse of Scripture that says we are accountable to God for our lives

blocks.label: Revision
blocks.text: Discuss the answers to the previous week’s questions.

blocks.label: Scripture Reading
blocks.text: Read Genesis 3:1-11 and ask questions about the difficult subjects.
God Wants: all people to have fellowship with Him, but when we sin and reject Him, that fellowship is broken.
Humankind Rejected God’s Word

When Eve began to listen to another voice, she began to go astray (Genesis 3:1-6). Adam and Eve rejected God because they did not believe what He said about the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, rather, they all listened to the serpent (the devil) and followed his deception while God was only gracious to them.
Humankind Did Not Let God Reign in Their Lives

Sin does not only mean doing what is evil, it also means not putting God first in your life, not believing in Him and not obeying Him. The first and greatest commandment is ‘Love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your mind and with all your strength’ (Mark 12:30). It is not murder or adultery that is the greatest sin, not allowing God to rule our lives is rather the greatest sin. The devil does everything he can to get us to dispute God and His word (Genesis 3: 1-4). As you live, if you do not pray and prayer does not matter to you, it means you have rejected God. If you are afraid of idols or witchcraft and cannot have faith in God that He can protect you, then it means that you have rejected God. If you think that a fetish priest or an amulet from a certain mallam can cure you, then you have rejected God. (Doctors, herbalists and many healers can help us, but as for the disease itself, it is God who heals.)
If We Reject God, We Get Under the Power of the Devil

Since humankind rejected God and the life He gives, they have been under the power of the devil (see Romans 1:28-32). Only the life of God can pull us out of this character described in the text we read.
Humankind Cannot Blame God for the Sins in Humans’ Life

No one cannot say, ‘That is how God created me so I cannot do anything about it’. God gave us the freewill in His own power to do what everyone wants, and therefore, if anyone sins, it is their own fault. Read James 1:13-15, Genesis 3:6
Rejecting God and His Word Leads to Death

God told Adam, ‘for when you eat from it you will certainly die’. Did Adam really die? Yes. Though, his body continued to live, his soul or character died. Adam and Eve were created in the image of God, capable of communicating with God happily. But because of their disobedience, they were separated from God and were expelled from the Garden of Eden. Spiritually, they died. So, have you ever tried to pray and you were unable to? Read Isaiah 59:1-4

verses.text: Behold, the LORD’s hand is not shortened, That it cannot save; Nor His ear heavy, That it cannot hear. But your iniquities have separated you from your God; And your sins have hidden His face from you, So that He will not hear.
For the wages of sin is death, but the gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord.

blocks.label: Discussion
blocks.text: Scripture says: We have all sinned (Romans 3:23) and have all died (Romans 5:12). Do you agree with it? And what about those in your church? What about the people in your city and country? So, are you really alive or are you separated from God and spiritually dead?

items: What can separate us from God?
How does the devil get us? (2 Corinthians 4:3-4)
Read Romans 1:28-32 again. Which of these things can you see in your own life?
Read Galatians 5:19-21. So will you inherit the kingdom of God or not?

lessons.title: God Has Given New Life in Jesus Christ

blocks.label: Revision
blocks.text: Discuss the answers to the previous week’s questions.

blocks.label: Scripture Reading
blocks.text: Read Isaiah 53:4-9 and Acts 13:26-31, 38-39 together and ask questions about what is difficult to understand.
God Has Not: said that sinners are sick only, but they also are dead. The dead can do nothing to help themselves – so if we die in sin, we cannot resurrect ourselves by our own strength.
Humankind Needs a Saviour
a. Without Christ, the spiritual forces we are fighting with are far stronger than we are – demons, spirits, charms,
sorcerers, and the devil himself (Ephesians 6:12).
b. We try to obey God’s laws, but we can never do good that pleases God and brings us into the kingdom of God (Romans 3:20).
c. Even if we can do good at times, we must be punished for the sins we have already committed (Romans 6:23).
d. When we begin to sin, it is very difficult to stop doing it by our own strength (John 8:34). Since we cannot win the battle in our own strength, we need someone to help us.
God Promised to Send a Saviour (Isaiah 53:4-9)

In Old Testament times, sinners used animals to pray for forgiveness and salvation. Many years before the birth of Jesus, Isaiah spoke of another sacrifice, not an animal, but ‘a man who will be afflicted’, whom he did not name. He said that an innocent man would be condemned (v. 9). He would be silent before his people (v. 7) and die (v. 8); he would bear the punishment we deserve (verses 4-6); and his sufferings would restore us (verse 5).
The Gospel: Jesus Came as Our Saviour (Acts 13:26-31)

Isaiah’s wonderful prophecy was fulfilled at the crucifixion of Jesus. He was blameless (Acts 13:28); He remained silent in front of the crowd (Matthew 27:12-14); died (Acts 13: 28-20); He bore our punishment, and by His suffering we can be healed (Isaiah 53:5). Most wonderfully, He rose from the dead (Acts 13:30-31) and is still alive – ‘He is able to save completely those who come to God through Him, because He always lives to intercede for them’ (Hebrews 7:25). This is called the ‘gospel’. How do you understand this gospel? It means that all our sins can be forgiven. We can start the great work God has created us for. We can have New Life because the risen Jesus will come to live with us.

verses.text: All we like sheep have gone astray; We have turned, every one, to his own way; And the LORD has laid on Him the iniquity of us all.
As newborn babes, desire the pure milk of the word, that you may grow thereby

blocks.label: Discussion
blocks.text: How can we believe that Isaiah 53 is really about Jesus?

items: Give two examples of how we cannot save ourselves
What benefits do we derive from the resurrection of Jesus?
Use your own words to describe the meaning of the gospel

lessons.title: Everyone Must Accept the New Life in Jesus

blocks.label: Revision
blocks.text: Discuss the answers to the questions from the previous week.

blocks.label: Scripture Reading
blocks.text: Read John 3:16; Mark 1:15 and John 15:1-5 and ask questions about what is difficult to understand.

JOHN 3:16 is the summary of the gospel. Firstly, it says that God has included all people in His plan of salvation. ‘For God so loved the world that He gave His only begotten Son’. But secondly, it says that only those who believe will receive the benefit of what He has done (John 3:16 does not promise us that all the world will have eternal salvation – except those who believe in Him’); The New Life is a gift: but one must accept the gift. It is like malaria treatment medicine in the hospital. You are given the medicine, and you have to take it. But it will not be beneficial to them unless they go to the clinic and admit that they have malaria before they are given medicine.
If You Turn Away from Sin, Then You Will Have New Life (Mark 1:15)

YOU CANNOT have the New Life in Jesus Christ unless you first turn away from selfishness and disobedience of the old life. Before you received New Life in Christ, you were dead in the sight of God: you received the New Life which required you to turn away from the old life. This will be difficult. Disobedience has become a habit for you, so when you are giving it up, you feel sad and as if you are dying. Paul says this: ‘I am crucified with Christ: nevertheless, I live; not I, but Christ lives in me’ (Galatians 2:20).

It may be stealing; it may be idolatry or witchcraft; perhaps you have neglected your husband, or your wife, or your children, or your family, or you have been arrogant or cruel to them; perhaps you have committed immorality in secret, or perhaps you have ignored God and have become pompous for violating a great commandment. It is difficult to repent – confess before God and man, ‘I am a sinner’ – but you must do this before you can have New Life.
You Will Have New Life When You Believe (Mark 1:15)

If you do not believe in Jesus Christ, you will not receive the New Life. Thousands of people believe in something about Jesus and think that it makes them Christians: but believing in something about a president of a nation does not make you a citizen of that nation, so does believing something about Jesus cannot make you a Christian – even the devil believes something about God (James 2:19).
To believe in Jesus is a different thing altogether. It means:
a. you will know that you need His forgiveness
b. you will know that He died to forgive you of your sin
c. you will ask for His forgiveness and believe that your sins are forgiven
d. you will decide that henceforth, you will give Him everything you have.
You Have New Life as You Have Received Him Into Your Life (John 1:12)
When you accept Jesus into your life and you let Him rule over you, you have New Life. A prayer from your heart can do this. A prayer like the following:

Lord Jesus, I need You. I know I have sinned so I am separated from You. I want to turn away from all my sins and follow You. I believe You died for me. Thank You for forgiving me my sin. Come into my life and rule over me until the day You will come and take me to be with You. I thank You, Lord, that You have heard my prayer as You promised.

The leader of the group should ensure that all those gathered should say the prayer. There may be people who have not made up their minds to accept Jesus Christ as Saviour and Lord. If they say this prayer properly, it will be a great thing in their lives. (Let them pray).
Then read Revelation 3:20. Have you truly called the Lord Jesus to come into your life at a certain time or place? If so, where is He according to the scriptures read?
Can I Be Sure That I Have New Life?

‘I have given up every sin I know. I truly believe that Jesus died for me. I have asked Him to forgive my sins and live with me forever. But I do not feel anything new inside. I cannot see that I have a whole New Life’. Do not rely on your feelings. Trust in the promise of God. Look for God’s promise in the following passage.
a. If we confess our sins, He is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness. (1 John 1:9).
b. Believe on the Lord Jesus, and you will be saved (Acts 16:31).
c. Behold, I stand at the door and knock. If anyone hears My voice and opens the door, I will come in to him and
eat with him, and he with Me (Revelation 3:20).

Study these three readings carefully. You will find that each one covers something that God requires of us and something that He promises us to do if we obey. If you have done your part, then trust that God has done His. And if you believe in God’s promise, the feelings you experience will confirm what God has done.

verses.text: If we confess our sins, He is faithful and just to forgive us our sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.
So they said, “Believe on the Lord Jesus Christ, and you will be saved, you and your household.”
Behold, I stand at the door and knock. If anyone hears My voice and opens the door, I will come in to him and eat with him, and he with Me.

blocks.label: Conclusion
blocks.text: Do you believe that everyone in the world will be saved? Give reasons? How would you respond to someone who asks you to receive New Life in Jesus? Can you really see that you have a New Life? If so, how do you know? If not, why not?

items: If we confess our sins to Jesus, what will He do?
What happens when we believe that Jesus died for us and accept what He did?
If we invite Him into our lives, what will He do?

lessons.title: We See New Life in Humankind’s Deeds

blocks.label: Revision
blocks.text: Discuss the answers to the questions from the previous week.

blocks.label: Scripture Reading
blocks.text: Read Ephesians 2:8-10 and Galatians 5:22-24 and ask questions about what is difficult to understand.

To Receive God’s: New Life is the greatest decision you can make. It is a decision that may, come suddenly or gradually – may come gradually – it is impossible to know when it happened. But there must be a time of change. Before that conversion, your life was going wrong: but what happened after your conversion?
You Have Been Saved to Bear Fruit (Galatians 5:22-25)

When you receive a New Life, the Spirit of God Himself will dwell in you. “Jesus said, ‘I am the vine, you are the branches’.” The purpose of the branches of a tree is to bear fruit, and if Jesus and the Spirit of God are to dwell in you, God requires that you see two kinds of fruit.
First, your life should be more progressive than before. Paul
calls this ‘the fruit of the Spirit’ (see Galatians 5:22-24).

Second, He seeks out for another Christian. Mango tree bears mangoes; palm tree bears palms; and the Christian can be recognised because he ‘bears’ a Christian – people living around them receive New Life in Christ.
You Were Saved to Serve (Ephesians 2:8-10)
It is wonderful to know Jesus as your Saviour and Friend but beware of two mistakes.
a. Many people think that salvation is the ultimate goal in
life: not so – it is what helps us to get what we want.
b. Many people think that God gives them New Life to satisfy themselves: but His purpose is more than this – He wants us to be useful to others.
Salvation is not the stage we live on: it is the channel that should lead us to the service of God. Immediately after Paul encountered the Lord Jesus on the road to Damascus, his
first question was, ‘What shall I do, Lord?’ (Acts 22:10).
What Happens If You Fall Back Into Sin?

If Christ lives in you, you must be able to live a good life. Unfortunately, we must admit that no Christian can ever be perfect: in fact, those who are with Christ admit that they are not perfect (1 John 1:8). If we sin, what can we do?

a. Do not hide it – confess it at once (remember the promise at 1 John 1:9). If it is raining and the driver does not use the wiper, soon the small droplets of water splashes on the windscreen will gradually accumulate and blur the view of the driver. Similarly, if you do not ask for forgiveness for small sins at once, soon your whole life will be destroyed.
b. Do not be overcome by evil – overcome it. It is better to regret what you have done. Reflect on the mistakes you have made, and then look at Philippians 4:8. Focus
on the positive things that can renew your mind.

c. Do not continue sinning – flee from it. If you continue to commit the same sins, it means you have not repented and accepted Christ in your life. It is true that our trials are so great for us - if we face these trials alone, we cannot succeed. But we are not alone in facing this challenge. Christians have Jesus living in them, they have New Life: ‘No one who is born of God will continue to sin, because God’s seed remains in them; they cannot go on sinning,
because they have been born of God’. (1 John 3:9).

verses.text: For we are His workmanship, created in Christ Jesus for good works, which God prepared beforehand that we should walk in them.
Whoever has been born of God does not sin, for His seed remains in him; and he cannot sin, because he has been born of God.

blocks.label: Discussion
blocks.text: As you have seen, is there a difference between Christians and churchgoers? So do our church members’ lifestyle fit the requirements of Galatians 5:22-24? Why do you think it’s not worth it?

items: Why did Jesus choose you (John 15:16)?
If you sin, is it better to give up?
What are the three things you should do if you sin?

blocks.text: Review of What Have Been Done

In Lessons 1-2, we learned what New Life is: we learned about God’s plan for the church to take the gospel of New Life to the world. We saw that God’s purpose is for every church and every Christian to be involved. In lessons 3-7, we learned the gospel – the truth of Christianity. You must be able to explain it to another person. Writing down the names
of lessons 3-7 will help you (the five pillars of the gospel) Preview of What Is to Be Done

In Lesson 8-9, we will study the messenger or witness – that is YOU! Are you fit to be a witness of Jesus to others? You know the overview of the gospel: but can you give it to others? You are a member of your church, but can you take the gospel out? You may be able to preach the gospel in your village or be a leader of the church; but do you believe that you are prepared to evangelise to the unbelievers?

lessons.title: The Witness Must Have the New Life

blocks.label: Revision
blocks.text: Review what you have learned in lessons 3-7

blocks.label: Scripture Reading
blocks.text: Read John 3:1-18 and ask questions about what is difficult to understand.
What Makes One a Good Witness?

IMAGINE that you are looking for a pair of good shoes. Two people recommend two different shoes. One said, ‘I have a degree in finance from the University of London. I have a business background. These shoes are advertised in the dailies and everyone says they are good shoes. I advise you to buy them’. The other is a labourer who has never been to school and says, ‘I bought shoes like this from this woman two years ago. See, I am still wearing these shoes right now – they have not worn out’. Which of these people is a good witness? Give reasons?
The Witness Must Have Experience

John 3:1-14 was about two people. One was a learned man, and a devout man: and he was a Pharisee, and a ruler of the Jews; (v. 1) and a teacher of Israel (v. 10). Maybe he was a good man, and he knew Old Testament religion. But he was not worthy to be a witness – he had not received God’s gift of New Life.

Everyone in the world has sinned – Nicodemus had also sinned, but his sin is pride and greed (not murder or adultery) so he did not know that he was a sinner. He did not realise that he has been separated from God. So Jesus said to him, ‘You need New Life: you must be born again! ‘The other person mentioned in John 3 is the same Jesus. Jesus is perfect when He bears witness: He says, ‘We speak that which we know, and bear witness of that which we have seen’ (John 3:11).
You Must Also Have Experience

If you want to be a witness and messenger of the New Life for all People, then you must be part of your church regularly and be a student of the Scriptures: but this is not all: you must have an experience of your Lord and Saviour: you must also have a New Life.

Many church members do not lead a Christ-like life. They do not tell the truth: they oppress the workers and their families; they are hypocrites, lazy or perverse. Some are smugglers; some are drunkards; others are greedy for profit. Such people cannot be witnesses for Jesus Christ – people will not take the gospel they preach seriously.
Other church members like Nicodemus should have lived a good life but have no experience of God. They have never seen;
i. that selfishness is sin,
ii. that sin separates them from God
ii. that they must confess their sins,
iii. that God has given them New Life,
iv. that they must receive a New Life,
v. that the New Life must be manifest in their lives.

Everyone will experience the New Life in different ways but if Jesus has not caused any change in their lives, they may ‘preach the gospel’ but they cannot bear witness. ‘Therefore, if anyone be in Christ, he is a new creature’ (2 Corinthians 5:17).
If You Want To Change Others, You Must First Experience Change
There is No Doubt
Lesson 6, point 4: ‘Can I believe that I have a New Life?’

You are teaching others to trust in God’s promise of forgiveness and salvation. You are going to tell them, if they have done their part (repented, placed their faith in Christ, and received Him into their lives), then they must acknowledge that God has also done His part.
Do you believe this yourself? They can be accepted. It must be accepted. If you were to be the messenger of the New Life to others, you have to know without a doubt that you have life.

verses.text: Jesus answered and said to him, “Most assuredly, I say to you, unless one is born again, he cannot see the kingdom of God.”
Therefore, if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation; old things have passed away; behold, all things have become new.

blocks.label: Discussion
blocks.text: Can the wicked receive New Life? Can one be a member of the church who is not ‘born again’? Have you openly confessed that you are a sinner and asked God to forgive you and save you? When someone is recommending something to you, what do you expect them to do?

items: Is eternal life is given to us in the future or right now? (See John 5:24 and 1 John 5:11-12)
Before one can receive a New Life, they must know that and put their trust. that was given to them.
List four things that you believe you will receive when you receive the New Life. Acts 10:43John 5:24 RomansJohn 14:1-3

blocks.label: Revision
blocks.text: Discuss the answers to the questions from the previous week.

blocks.label: Scripture Reading
blocks.text: Read Acts 8:26-40 and ask questions about what is difficult to understand.

The WITNESS must not only receive New Life; they must also prepare themselves to share with others. How can you prepare yourself? We trust that this booklet is helping you, and we believe that your study leader is a good teacher: but you cannot be well organised unless you have a very good teacher, and you learn from a wonderful book.
Philip Relied on the Holy Spirit (Acts 8:26:30)

Philip committed himself to God and was filled with the Holy Spirit (Acts 6:3,5). He lived and testified of Jesus in the power of the Spirit. We must be filled with the Spirit (Ephesians 5:18) and bear witness in His power. When the Holy Spirit empowers us and controls our lives, we can bear fruit (Zechariah 4:6).

Philip was a man of prayer. Prayer is talking to your teacher: not asking for something in vain – it also means listening and paying attention to what God is saying to you. In today’s reading, look for two signs that Philip heard God speaking to him.

Philip listened to his teacher. Look again at the two passages you have seen: Did Philip do what he was told? Only the Spirit of God knows who has opened their heart to listen to the gospel of the New Life. You must listen to what God is saying to you and speak to those whom God has sent to you, as Philip did.
Philip Trusted God’s Word (Acts 8:31-35)

The Holy Scriptures were Philip’s study, and he was well acquainted with Old Testament theology. Suppose you met someone reading the Scriptures – perhaps Ezekiel or Titus: – do you know the Scriptures well enough to understand them, or would you know where they were in the Scriptures? The Holy Scriptures is a long book. If you want to understand it better, you have to read it carefully. Set aside time each day to study the Scriptures, and never let it go to waste. Christian literature, such as the Light of Our Way or Eternal Guidance will help you.

Philip spoke to the Ethiopian from the Holy Scriptures. It is better to tell others about your relationship with Christ than to speak in your own words: because the Word of God has the unique power to give light and understanding (Psalm 119:130), to teach and to correct (2 Timothy 3:16).

A witness must know the main chapters of Scripture and their location: he or she must be able to choose the appropriate reading for the person to whom they he or she is speaking and learn to read at will. Philip used the Scriptures to explain Jesus. There is no point in talking about another life unless you talk about Jesus: show how He died, and how He rose from the death. ‘Faith cometh by hearing, and hearing by the word of God’ (Romans 10:17, KJV). Never despise any denomination: but ‘from every scripture preach Jesus Christ’ (Acts 8:35).
Philip Led the Ethiopian to Make a Decision

The Ethiopian saw that it was not enough to talk about Jesus or to agree with Philip on what he was saying. He thought about taking this New Life for himself. He asked to be baptised in a symbol of repentance and a new conversion. Similarly, all who wants to become a Christian must turn away from their old ways: they must know that Jesus was led as a sheep to the slaughter and believe that Jesus did it for them. They must pray and understand and make the risen Jesus the ‘Saviour of the World’ and their Saviour.
If you want to be a messenger of New Life like Philip, you should not only tell what you have learned in this lesson to others, you must also help yourself and lead others to find
their answer. We will learn more about this in lesson 11.

verses.text: For as many as are led by the Spirit of God, these are sons of God.
So then faith comes by hearing, and hearing by the word of God.

A witness must have the New Life – do you have the New Life? You want to change others – are you changed yourself? Have you turned away from anything that is displeasing to God in your life and accepted the forgiveness of Christ?
If not, examine yourself now and cast away any known sin: and ask Jesus to be your Saviour and Lord henceforth.

A witness must be prepared – are you prepared? Do you want the power to speak the gospel – have you asked the Spirit of God to dwell in you? Do you want to use the Scriptures to help others – are you ready to study the Scriptures daily? My Pledge

So I give myself to You, take me and use me in any way You desire. Please fill me with Your Spirit. Prepare me to be a good witness. Use me and all Christians to spread Your word throughout my community, my country, and beyond. Amen.

lessons.title: How to Share the Gospel with People

blocks.label: Revision
blocks.text: Discuss the pledge written previous lesson, and what it means.
YOU are dedicated to God: you want to be His messenger: and He wants you to do His work.
How Can You Spread the Word?

a. By Actions (Acts 20:18): We must preach with our mouth and our life. If your life does not match what you say, you will confuse people. But if you are filled with the Spirit of God and people see the fruit of the Spirit in your actions, then you have ‘spoken’ before you even open your mouth. (See Galatians 5:22-23).

b. By Conversation: Christians are often not afraid to talk about their faith. Some Christians are afraid that others will say they are weird. But supporters of Football teams such as Asante Kotoko or Accra Hearts of Oak, Manchester United or Liverpool are not afraid to discuss football; drinkers are not ashamed to talk about alcohol. Christians have a reason to talk about the Saviour. Are you doing it? How will you start?

c. By Your testimony: (See Paul’s testimony in Acts 22 and 26). Do not just talk about the church or Christianity for nothing. If Jesus has done something in your life, talk about Him and tell what He has done for you.

d. Through Books: There are places you cannot go but books can go. Of the 27 books in the New Testament, 21 are personal letters. Can you write down what Jesus has done for you and send to others? You cannot preach the gospel continuously, but a booklet can tell the story for months or even years. You know where they sell Christian literature. Try and get Christian books and sell to your friends.
If you like a book, others will like it too.
Where Can You Spread the Word?
a. In your own home: Invite a few friends to your home and study the Scriptures or meet with one of the elders of your church.

b. In the homes of others (Acts 20:20): Paul went from house to house. You can do the same. Tell them who you are and why you have come: ‘I am Kofi Asare from The Church of Pentecost. I want to tell you something about the Life for All People. Do you have time to listen to me? ‘
Here are guidelines on what can be done after this:
i. tell them how you received the New Life.
ii. explain to them that God has given New Life to everyone.
iii. invite them to meetings in your house or church.
iv. read a word from Scripture and explain it briefly.

c. At school, at work and everywhere: Let everyone know that Jesus has changed your life and is still helping you every day. ‘If anyone asks you why you believe, be anxious to answer him’ (1 Peter 3:15). When you travel in a bus or go shopping, carry small gospel tracts; it will help you to communicate with others.

d. Street preaching: With a few people from your church alone or gather a few people from the various churches in the city, perhaps in a youth group or a women’s group. Near the religious temple, or the marketplace, or the square. If the meeting is large, police permission must be requested. The preacher should emphasise the five pillars of Christ’s word.
Guidelines to Spreading the Word of God
a. Pray before you speak: Name people and pray for them.
b. Humble yourself (Acts 20:19): Never speak against another church. Listen to what people say and be patient
with insults; also, never argue or become angry.

c. Let the love of Christ rule over you: Jesus loved many of the people of Jerusalem and when He saw the punishment and suffering that would come upon them, He wept. Paul made his ministry so important that when he thought about it, he wept. (Luke 19:41; Acts 20:19; compare Psalm 126:6).
d. Write down your activities: Write down the visits you have made and keep records of them. Afterwards, pray for the people you have spoken to.

lessons.title: How to Let People Know Jesus

blocks.text: Summary: Discuss the answers to the questions from the previous week.

blocks.label: Scripture Reading
blocks.text: Read Ephesians 3:7-9 and 14-17. Verses 7-9 describe your task of leading people to Jesus: you can use verses 14-17 to pray for those you are going to help.

We Learned In Lesson 6: that ‘everyone must receive New Life in Jesus’. This course will help you advise those who want to know. When you witness at work, at school, from house to house, or at special church meetings, people will say to themselves, ‘Of course, I need Jesus too’. You should always seek this person: and you should help yourself to counsel them and lead them to Jesus.
Four Rules for the Counsellor

a. Pray about the work earnestly. If you ask God to help you, you will be able to help someone to make an informed choice that will have great impact in their life. If you belittle yourself, you will delay the work God is doing in you.
b. Present people to Jesus and not the church. Do not tell them the church you attend. Show them the Saviour on whose side you are.
c. Do not discuss with people the secrets or experiences they shared with you while advising them. These are the matters between them and the Lord alone.
d. If you are a man, try to advise men and let a woman advise women. A man may not be able to help a woman well and vice versa.
Find Out What the Questioner is Thinking

You are talking to someone who has a personal need and issue so befriend him or her well and talk to him or her as a friend. Shake hands as you would do anywhere. Introduce yourself to them and ask their name.

Then ask them why they would want to talk to you. Make no suggestions to them – let them reveal their own words to you. Make sure you understand their needs before you consider a solution, otherwise they will get confused in their mind.

a. There are people who, for the sake of gossip or because they are just looking for a book, will come to you. Try to let these people know what Jesus has done for them and encourage them to start reading the Scriptures regularly; but do not think that they are ready to give their lives to Jesus.

b. Some will come for marital advice. Students will tell you their academic challenges. Workers will bring their job difficulties. Witchcraft and idolatry would be troubling others. In whichever case, Jesus can help but the questioner may not see this at the beginning. So it is better to spend a little time to discuss their challenges; then tell them that if they accept Jesus into their lives, He will help them find a solution.

c. Some will truly understand that they need Jesus, but they do not know what they are doing. They will say, ‘I want to be a true Christian’, or ‘I want to live a good life’. Some will feel very guilty about the sins they have committed.
Teach such persons ‘the five (5) principles of the gospel’ (lessons 3 through 7, especially lessons 4, 5 and 6).
i. Let them know they have rejected God’s gift of life
ii. Are they prepared to stay away from sin?
iii. Are they ready to believe in Jesus?
iv. Are they ready to invite Jesus into their lives?

Never force someone to make a decision. If you cannot see that a person is ready, say to him or her, ‘Go and pray about it; make up your mind at home; then come and tell me what you have done (or write me a letter)’. This is better than forcing them to take a decision which they have not thought of. However, by the grace of God, some will be ready to talk to God, confess their sins, ask for forgiveness and give their lives to Him.

d. Some will be Christians who have turned away from Christ and want to return to Him. Help these people to understand that, those who confess their sins to God will be forgiven (1 John 1:8-9) and can overcome temptation (1 Corinthians 10:13; Romans 6:14).
Use Your Bible

We learned in Lesson 9 that studying the Scriptures is very important in your preparation. If you learn to read and memorise them, you can choose to recite them for each person’s needs. So, in your conversation, you must speak on the basis of the power of God’s word: You must open the Scriptures and read them together with the questioner; and if necessary, write down the quotations for them – it will help in the discussion.
Establish Contact With The Questioner For Further Contact
When counselling a seeker, think of yourself as a rescuer and them as another baby who will need your help a few weeks after birth.
a. Do not let the questioner go without writing their name and place of residence and you giving yours to them. Find out where they live and work.
b. Invite them to your home for fellowship, prayers, and Scripture reading. Christianity in your home will help them more than telling them many religious things. Visit them in their homes too.
c. If it is difficult to visit, often write to and send them some gospel tracts.
d. Show them a good book and lend yours. Show them a good school where they can learn to write (and if they have never learned anything like this, then you should do something to see how it happens).
e. Communicate with them in prayer. Pray for the poor regularly and mention them in prayer-remember Ephesians 3:14-17

lessons.title: How to Disciple People in the Church

blocks.label: Revision
blocks.text: Discuss the answers to the questions from the previous week.

blocks.label: Scripture Reading
blocks.text: Read Colossians 3:1-16 and ask questions about difficult matters.

We Learned: in Lesson 7 that salvation is not the ultimate goal of life but its beginning. It will be your job to help other Christians grow and continue in the Christian life. What Paul said in Colossians 3 and 4 can be learned from other Christians who are coming to church.
New Goals (Vv. 1-2)

Before Jesus Christ became your Lord, what was your main goal in life? What is your goal right now? Help other Christians to find new goals in life. If their goals do not change, then their Master has not changed either.
Continue to Repent (Verses 5-11)

When a person first repents, they cast off all known sin. Later, they see many things in their life that must change - things that they never thought were wrong before. Repentance is a fighting thing; we must always be in it, throughout our lives. So, the Colossians were already Christians and already repented, but Paul had to say to them, ‘Put to death the uncleanness of your mind’.
New Deeds (Verses 12-15)
Put On – The new Christian should not think that the Christian life is something they should stop doing; there are other things they must do, good things they could not do before.
New Book (V. 16)

The new Christian will find the Scriptures more interesting than the former – the Scriptures have not changed, but they have changed! How can the word of Christ dwell in you ‘richly’? To continue to read the Holy Scriptures regularly. See to it that the converts read regularly ‘Light of our way’ or ‘Eternal Guidance’. You too follow along as you can see them reading and ask them each time you meet, what did you read this morning? What did you learn from it?
Ernest in Prayer (4:2-4)

Every one of us has what we do every day including work, eating, sleeping, relaxing, bathing and so much more. If the new Christian is to make an effort to pray, they must include prayer in their daily routine. Many people love the early morning. But whenever they do, this new Christian must
make time for regular prayer and study of the Scriptures.

Teach them to say their prayer properly: not ‘God bless my church’, but ‘Help the pastor as he prepares for this coming Sunday’s sermon, when he will settle the matter between the singer and the choirmaster. Teach me what you want me to do at church’. Tell them when they pray for people, they should mention their names.
New Oneness (3:15-16 and Ephesians 2: 17-22)

In the past, they might have been one with people at drinking spots. Now, you have to bring them to church. This will require changes on both sides. The new Christian will immediately fit into the church because Christ is transforming them; but the church must also change. Will converts find confidence in women’s groups, men’s groups, youth groups, or fellowship meetings? Look for the organisation of these groups during the half year – will the new Christians get the help and benefits they need, if they attend the scheduled meetings?

Some of these converts will need baptism. Your church must organise training for the elders who handle convert who need baptism. But ensure that this meeting does not drive these converts away from the daily life of the church. They need to be one with you this time. Working with them in this study will help them.
New Family (3:11, 18-21)
We have a new family with Christ, and this has led us to belong to a new family with other people. The new Christian should repent of their old deeds.
New Work Attitude (3:17, 22-25)

The Christian worships two masters – the master of earthly works and the Lord of heaven. This passage teaches us that we should not do our daily work to please our employers, but to please the Lord. You may say, “But I am a labourer, typist or a messenger. I cannot do this for the Lord. The Bible emphasizes that you must do every work as if you were doing it to please God for it is more acceptable to do the work of God than to please others.

verses.text: Now, therefore, you are no longer strangers and foreigners, but fellow citizens with the saints and members of the household of God
And whatever you do, do it heartily, as to the Lord and not to men

blocks.label: Conclusion
blocks.text: Christ’s death has already reconciled the Colossians with God (Colossians 1:22). Why did Paul tell them to put to death the evil in them? Have they not already repented? If you go to church regularly, you need to pray and read ‘The Holy Scriptures’ forever? If so, why? In what ways does your church refuse to welcome converts into its unity?

items: In our group, we have divisions in language, financial strength, education and many other things. Should these be against the family relations among Christians?. What verse or passage answers these questions?..
It will be your duty to teach this lesson to the new Christians. Which of these eight principles stated above must you learn for yourself first?
There are some works you cannot do for God. If so, what are these?
What advice should you give to a Christian in such a job?
